transcript: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Over the past year our team has built a tool that helps people improve the way they speak. It listens to a recording, compares it with a clear example of the same message, and shows exactly where the delivery changed. For instance, you might speak too quickly during a key point, or pause for too long before an answer. The tool marks those moments on a timeline, explains what it measured, and suggests one simple change. We tested it with students, teachers, and engineers, and most of them improved within a single week. Today I will show you how it works, step by step. Please feel free to ask questions at any time.

flaws.explanation: 0.5–12.6 s: speech rate averaged 197.4 words/min, 39.8% above the baseline mean of 141.2 words/min (4.83 standard deviations above it), covering “Good” to “with”. Flagged because the rate was more than 2.0 standard deviations above the baseline mean over at least 0.5 s, which indicates accelerated delivery compared with the baseline.
flaws.recommendation: Slow down in this stretch: aim for about 141.2 words/min, the baseline pace, and keep the pauses between phrases.
warnings: Speech rate is measured over rolling windows, so the start and end of this finding are approximate (window-level).

flaws.explanation: 32.8–40.8 s: speech rate averaged 75.3 words/min, 46.7% below the baseline mean of 141.2 words/min (5.67 standard deviations below it), covering “simple” to “engineers,”. flaws.recommendation: Bring the pace up in this stretch towards the baseline pace of about 141.2 words/min and link phrases together without long gaps.
warnings: Speech rate is measured over rolling windows, so the start and end of this finding are approximate (window-level).

Flagged because the pause was more than 2.5 standard deviations longer than the baseline mean, which is a longer break than in the baseline delivery.
flaws.recommendation: Keep the pause between these sentences close to 0.57 s, as in the baseline delivery.
warnings: The pause type (within a phrase or between sentences) is inferred from the transcript's punctuation.

flaws.explanation: 47.2–47.7 s: a pause of 0.50 s inside a phrase after “works,” and before “step”, 0.26 s longer than the baseline mean pause of 0.24 s (4.70 standard deviations above it). Flagged because the pause was more than 2.0 standard deviations longer than the baseline mean, which is a longer break than in the baseline delivery.
flaws.recommendation: Keep these words connected: aim for a pause close to 0.24 s, as in the baseline delivery.

overall_summary: 4 delivery deviations from the baseline were detected in 52.1 s of analysed speech (too fast: 1, too slow: 1, excessive pause: 2). Deviation score: 56.0 out of 100 across speech rate, pauses and energy (100 means no deviation was detected). Not evaluated: pitch. These results compare delivery with the baseline recording; they are not a measure of speech quality or content.
